digest: MDN directly confirms that AbortSignal.timeout() cannot be cancelled, and documents listener/GC and active-time caveats.
verdictDigest: MDN explicitly states that AbortSignal.timeout() provides no cancellation mechanism and recommends AbortController with setTimeout()/clearTimeout() for definitive early cancellation. Source: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/AbortSignal/timeout_static

evidence.quote: AbortSignal.timeout() does not provide a way to cancel its timeout.
The AbortSignal becoming unreachable is not guaranteed to cancel the timeout.
evidence.relevance: Clarifies that garbage collection or losing references does not reliably cancel the timeout.

evidence.quote: The timeout is based on active rather than elapsed time, and will effectively be paused if the code is running in a suspended worker, or while the document is in a back-forward cache (“bfcache”).
evidence.relevance: Documents an important lifecycle and timing caveat.

caveats: While pending, abort listeners can keep the signal alive and prevent garbage collection; remove listeners when no longer needed.
For definitive early cancellation, MDN recommends AbortController with setTimeout() and clearTimeout().
